name: OpenFlux
description: Network stack research tool. TCP tunnel with pluggable transports.
one_liner: A tool that disguises your internet traffic as normal messaging-app traffic so it can slip past network blocks in restrictive countries.
buyer: No legitimate commercial buyer — the project explicitly disclaims commercial use, and its function (disguising traffic to bypass network restrictions) is a censorship-circumvention tool for individuals, not a business.
business_use_cases: None fit standard business use — it exists specifically to route around network-level blocking, which is outside normal commercial application.
A network-security researcher could study its transport-disguising techniques to improve legitimate DPI-detection or firewall products.
A digital-rights nonprofit might reference or fund similar open tools as part of free-speech/censorship-resistance advocacy, funded by grants rather than sales.

money_ideas.idea: None recommended for direct commercialization — the project is explicitly non-commercial by its own disclaimer.

steal_this: Not a viable weekend business idea — it's a non-commercial research/circumvention tool with real legal risk in the jurisdictions it targets.
